comparator.name: Ancient Studies — Oude Geschiedenis specialization
comparator.sourceNotes: OER 2026–2027, Articles 10.2 and 11.1–11.6, distinguishes the Dutch Oudheidwetenschappen trajectory from the English Ancient Studies trajectory. The Dutch trajectory's Oude Geschiedenis specialization is selected neutrally as the broadest historical route, not because of UCR offerings. The 180-EC pathway contains eight compulsory introductory units (48 EC), two coherent restricted orientation electives (12 EC), eight compulsory postpropedeutic units (48 EC), five compulsory Oude Geschiedenis specialization units (30 EC), 30 EC of genuinely free minor/elective space in year three and a compulsory 12-EC bachelor thesis including colloquium. The orientation electives instantiate Classical Mythology and Seminar Ancient History, both permitted by Article 11.4; the year-three open choice remains unfilled. The 0-EC language diagnostic does not enter the credit total. The official prospectus presents illustrative year-by-year courses rather than an exhaustive credit-bearing list; the OER governs EC and status.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the generic Dutch-taught Oudheidwetenschappen bachelor, not a specialization. Article 10.2 of the 2026–2027 OER confirms the Dutch trajectory's five current formal specializations: Oude Geschiedenis, Oude Nabije Oosten, Archeologie, Grieks and Latijn. A specialization is required (Article 11.1). Oude Geschiedenis ranges across the Ancient Near East, Rome, antiquity's politics and international relations, social history and world heritage; it is the broadest general historical coverage. The others specialize in a particular region, material/field method or ancient language and literature. The choice follows the least-specialized route rule independently of UCR fit. It is the OER's first-listed Dutch specialization as well.

programmes.label: Ancient Studies — Oude Geschiedenis specialization at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

exception.reason: This bachelor develops integrated specialist knowledge of ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern history, ancient written and material sources, religion and philosophy, reception and heritage, and a five-course Oude Geschiedenis specialization with a field excursion and historical research thesis. UCR has a handful of substantive courses in world and Greek archaeology, Greek democracy, myth and literature, ancient influences on political philosophy and comparative empires. Its other history, art, literature and museum courses primarily concern later eras or different regions. No 24-course UCR programme can preserve the historical core and specialist methods of this exact ancient-studies target without presenting modern history, unrelated heritage, contemporary politics or general literary theory as ancient-world study.
exception.curriculumContext: The 2026–2027 adopted OER confirms both language trajectories and the exact Dutch Oude Geschiedenis specialization. This pathway chooses two allowed 6-EC orientation subjects, keeps the 30-EC third-year minor/free elective space open, and includes the 12-EC thesis. The university's prospective-student page shows different sample specializations and cannot establish their credit weights; the OER supplies the formal structure.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Checked the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (151 rows), examining actual descriptions, outline-derived profiles, prerequisites and semester availability. MCCHEAM112 covers world archaeology through and beyond antiquity; MCCHEAM213 treats Greek archaeology and early democracy; MCCHEAM315 treats ancient heritage and democracy; MCCLITR211 compares ancient myths; GOSHIST213 includes warfare from antiquity onward; GOSHIST211 compares empires across eras; GOSPOLI111 discusses classic political thinkers; GOSPHIL111 has historical philosophical foundations. GOSHIST312 develops historical research but uses a Napoleonic Walcheren case. These courses offer real partial overlaps, yet UCR has no ancient-language study, dedicated Near Eastern history, systematic Greek/Roman historical sequence, archaeological field school, ancient source training or equivalent thesis course. Filling the remaining 24-course schedule would require many courses on modern art, modern history, contemporary politics and media that do not implement the ancient-world closest-match concept.
